Question B-006-003-011.

Why the correct answer is right: Foam dielectric lowers dielectric loss and usually gives a higher velocity factor than solid polyethylene. That is why a foam version of a coax family may have lower attenuation.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Higher power handling": Solid dielectric often handles heat and mechanical stress better, so higher power handling is not the primary advantage of foam.
- sourceIndex 2: "Lower velocity factor": Foam normally raises velocity factor because more of the dielectric is air; lower velocity factor states the trend backward.
- sourceIndex 3: "Better mechanical stability": Foam can deform or allow conductor movement more readily than solid dielectric, so mechanical stability is not its main advantage.
